y-m-61-02.material: Study f(x)=|x−1|/(x−1), x≠1. (|x−1| absolute value of x minus 1.) Denominator at x=1 is 0, so undefined. Values shown gradually.

y-m-61-02.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Changing f(1) doesn't change nearby values. Limit determined only by nearby values.
y-m-61-02.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Limit depends on values near 1, so redefining f(1) doesn't change it.
y-m-61-02.s.s1.st.2.r.d: You use fact limit depends on nearby values, not value at x=1.
y-m-61-02.s.s1.reflect: How did confidence change from right-side-only to both sides? In one sentence, why can't redefining f(1) affect limit?

y-m-61-05.material:
We want find instantaneous rate of change (derivative) of function f(x)=x³ (x³ mean 'x cubed') at x=1. We calculate average rate of change A(h)=(f(1+h)−f(1))/h while we make h smaller. (h na nonzero number.)
h | 1 | 0.5 | 0.1 | 0.01
A(h) | 7 | 4.75 | 3.31 | 3.0301
Seoyun: "When h=0.1 e be 3.31, so f′(1)=3.31." Dojun: "As h dey smaller e dey approach 3, so I think say f′(1)=3."

y-m-61-05.s.s1.r.a: E take average rate of change when h=0.1 directly as instantaneous rate of change. Check how the value change in table as h dey smaller.
y-m-61-05.s.s1.o.b: Dojun correct. The last value 3.0301 close to 3, so e don confirm say f′(1)=3.
y-m-61-05.s.s1.r.b: Being close to 3 and being exactly 3 different. 3.0301 na only the last value.
y-m-61-05.s.s1.o.c: Dojun 3 na only estimate, e never confirm; and Seoyun 3.31 na only one value when h=0.1.
y-m-61-05.s.s1.r.c: E compare evidence for both claims and separate estimation from confirmation.
y-m-61-05.s.s1.o.d: Both wrong. The values in table dey change, so we no fit determine f′(1).
y-m-61-05.s.s1.r.d: Even if values dey change, if dem dey gather round one number, you fit estimate am. Check whether dem dey gather.
y-m-61-05.s.s1.explain: A(h) dey come close to 3 with 7, 4.75, 3.31, 3.0301. Dojun 3 na convincing estimate, but from the four table values alone we no fit confirm say f′(1) exactly 3. Seoyun 3.31 na just average rate of change when h=0.1.

y-m-61-05.s.s2.fail.c1: Make h nonzero with absolute value at most 1, abeg.

y-m-61-05.s.s2.fail.c2: The difference between A(h) and 3 na 0.05 or more. Try h wey smaller.
y-m-61-05.s.s2.explain: A(h)=((1+h)³−1)/h=3+3h+h², so A(h)−3=3h+h². If |h| less than 0.016, the difference less than 0.05, and negative h fit work too. With h=0.1 and −0.1, the differences na 0.31 and 0.29, wey big.

y-m-61-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You write say A(h) fit be written as expression in h?

y-m-61-05.s.s3.model.2: By derivative definition, you fit find limit lim A(h), or use (x³)′=3x², to confirm say f′(1)=3.

y-m-61-08.topic: Tangent line equation: tangents through point outside curve
y-m-61-08.goal: When finding tangents through a point not on curve, explain why can't assume point's x-coordinate is tangency point; find tangency x-values and show two possible tangents.
y-m-61-08.material:
Curve y=x² and point A(1,−3). Find lines through A tangent to curve.
Hansol solution: "Derivative y=x² is 2x, so slope at x=1 is 2. Line through A with slope 2 is y=2(x−1)−3=2x−5. This is the only tangent."
